newsitem.title: UK: Asia attracts up to 500,000 tonnes Russian gas oil.
newsitem.headline: Asia attracts up to 500,000 tonnes Russian gas oil.

text.p: The European gas oil market is poised on a knife edge balancing between glut and drought, oil traders warned on Tuesday.
"If all the Russian (supply) that has been fixed eastwards goes, then it's going to get tight here (in Europe)," said one trader.
But, if the strong Asian market slumps because of the advancing gas oil armada, the situation could quickly be reversed, other market players said.
Estimates varied slightly, but there is a consensus that up to 500,000 tonnes of Russian gas oil could be headed to India and Singapore from the Black Sea and Baltic.
In addition the Middle East is sending substantial amounts of gas oil to the Asian market where prices are supported by refinery turnarounds and relatively strong refining margins.
Since the beginning of March gas oil traders have seen the possibility of arbitraging eastwards and have been fixing vessels to pick up cargoes from March 10 onwards.

Some traders felt the Singapore market will bow under the pressure of incoming product set to arrive in early April, which may force traders with cargoes about to load or already on the water to think twice.
"It still looks good in the short-term and the only real problem is finding freight," said one trader who assessed the longer-term outlook for the Europe eastwards arb as less rosy.
Hong Kong traders are understood to be looking for diesel
following strong selling into Southern China, but are holding back in the hope of picking up cheaper barrels with the arrival of European and Middle East material.

The spread between Russian prompt cif NWE gas oil against Singapore gas oil stands at a touch over $35 a tonne, and although freight costs have risen in recent weeks, shipping brokers say a 60,000 tonne cargo should be able to secure carriage to Singapore out of Europe at about $25 a tonne.

The prospect of Russian gas oil moving eastwards has pushed premiums higher in Europe. Traders say premiums on Tuesday were around April IPE +$2-3 cif NWE compared with -$1 against the March contract a couple of weeks ago.
